glosses: Both detectable and at least modestly substantial: large enough to be estimated and to be of practical relevance.

examples.text: For many people, the benefits of exercise in improving mood and preventing achiness are appreciable.
A grain of musk will scent a drawer for many years, and still lose nothing appreciable of its original weight.
For an appreciable time he did not think of rising from his seat.

Anti-freeze has not been found necessary, even in the most severe conditions, since the water is drained out if a locomotive spends any appreciable time out of service and in normal working conditions the coolant is always warm.
If NEAsia were a zone of peace, those American forces would be unnecessary and they could be sent home and demobilized, saving the U.S. taxpayer an appreciable sum of money.
A small hernia was just barely appreciable upon palpation.

translations.source_sense_description: so, dass es sich erkennen lässt; deutlich wahrnehmbar

glosses: Capable of being seen or noticed.

examples.text: The dismissal of a player who left Arsenal for Manchester City before joining Tottenham gave the home players and fans a noticeable lift.

Even in an era when individuality in dress is a cult, his clothes were noticeable. He was wearing a hard hat of the low round kind favoured by hunting men, and with it a black duffle-coat lined with white.

translations.source_sense_description: so, dass es sich erkennen lässt; deutlich wahrnehmbar

examples.text: Même s’ils sont plus ou moins fréquentés, les espaces verts de la cité angérienne sont appréciés… et appréciables.

glosses: Qui peut être apprécié par les sens ou avec le secours des procédés physiques ; dont on peut évaluer le poids, l’intensité, la durée, etc.

examples.text: Cette quantité est si petite qu’elle n’est pas appréciable.
Un son appréciable.
